spec: Define select_jobs(data). Input data is a list of at most 12 jobs, each [start, end, profit] with integer values and start < end. Select a subset whose half-open intervals [start, end) do not overlap; touching endpoints are allowed. The empty subset is allowed. Maximize total profit, then minimize selected job count, then choose the lexicographically smallest ascending list of original zero-based job indices. Return that ascending list. Do not modify the input.

Define match_path(data). Input data is a dictionary with pattern and text, both ASCII strings of at most 30 characters. Return a bool indicating whether the entire text matches the entire pattern. Slash / is the path separator. An unescaped ? matches exactly one non-slash character. An unescaped * matches zero or more non-slash characters. Each maximal consecutive unescaped run of at least two stars matches zero or more characters, including slash. Backslash escapes the next character, making it literal; a final backslash is literal. Every other character, including brackets and dot, is literal. Do not modify the input.

Define best_itinerary(data). Input data is a dictionary with flights, start, goal, and time. flights is a list of at most 12 flights [origin, destination, departure, arrival]; origin and destination, start, and goal are ASCII city strings, and departure, arrival, and time are integers with departure < arrival for every flight. A route starts in start with its first departure >= time; each subsequent flight has origin equal to the previous destination and departure >= the previous arrival. The last destination must equal goal. Waiting and repeated cities are allowed. Rank routes by earliest final arrival, then fewest flights, then lexicographically smallest sequence of original zero-based flight indices in travel order. If start == goal return []; otherwise return the best route as a list of original zero-based flight indices in travel order, or None if no route exists. Do not modify the input.
